svg.title: Minor sixth (m6): information sheet
svg.desc: Minor sixth, m6: C4 to A♭4, 8 semitones. A keyboard from C4 to C5 with both keys highlighted in this interval's identity colour and 8 numbered semitone hops. Two time strips show the notes one after another and together. Plogger [8] lens: Modal family (rounded), → Octave, Non-harmonic (Plogger), dense/dark.

g.text: 6 letter names counted inclusively (C to A)
HOW TO READ THE THREE PLOGGER MARKS
perfect-group family. A family label, not a
A historic teaching lens from the archived
acoustic law. The identity colour is a separate,
Next lower: Perfect fifth (P5, 7 semitones). Root C4 stays; upper note A♭4→G4, one key apart.
Plogger: A changes, B same, C changes.
Next higher: Major sixth (M6, 9 semitones). Root C4 stays; upper note A♭4→A4, one key apart.
Plogger: A same, B same, C changes.
How to read: find C4 on your keyboard, then count 8 semitones up (every key, white or
black, is one step) to A♭4. The numbered arcs are those steps. Top left shows the two
notes one after another, top right the same two notes together.
